Trim
trim
v.t. (to put in order; to dress; to adjust)
Old English trymman, to strengthen or set in order. The Authorized Version uses it three times, and the range is remarkable: a beard left untrimmed in loyalty, a nation trimming its way to seek love, and ten virgins trimming their lamps at midnight.

Biblical Definition

Mephibosheth's untrimmed beard is a legal argument. When David returned, Mephibosheth “had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came again in peace” (2 Samuel 19:24) — his body was the evidence that he had not celebrated the king's exile. Jeremiah uses the verb for a very different grooming: “Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love? therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways” (Jeremiah 2:33). Judah dressed up her conduct to attract lovers, and became so skilled at it that she instructed the wicked. The third use is the parable: “Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps” (Matthew 25:7). All ten trimmed; the trimming was not the difference. Five had oil and five had none, and the lamps of the foolish went out precisely when they were finally attended to. Preparation that begins at the cry is too late.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines trim as to make right; to put in due order; to dress; to decorate; and, of a lamp, to snuff or clean for burning.

expand to see more

TRIM, v.t. To make right, neat or pleasing; to adjust; to put in due order the parts of a thing.

TRIM, v.t. To dress; to decorate; to invest or embellish with extra ornaments.

TRIM, v.t. To make trim; as, to trim a lamp, that is, to snuff or clean the wick.

TRIM, v.i. To balance; to fluctuate between parties, so as to appear to favor each.

LAMP, n. A vessel with a wick, used for the combustion of oil or other inflammable substance, for the purpose of producing light.

Key Scripture

2 Samuel 19:24 — "And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, and had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came again in peace."

Jeremiah 2:33 — "Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love? therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways."

Matthew 25:7 — "Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps."

Matthew 25:8 — "And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out."

Modern Corruption

Presentation has become the main labour of religion — ways trimmed to be found attractive — while the parable warns that every lamp can be trimmed at midnight and only the ones with oil keep burning.

expand to see more

Jeremiah 2:33 names a temptation the church has never outgrown: trimming the way to seek love. The verb is about grooming conduct for an audience, making the path look attractive to the ones whose favour is wanted, and the prophet adds the sting — a people who become expert at it end up teaching the wicked ones their ways. A ministry that arranges its doctrine, its language and its emphases by what will be well received has not merely compromised; it has become an instructor in compromise for anyone watching.

Matthew 25 exposes the deeper danger, which is that trimming is indistinguishable from readiness right up to the moment it matters. All ten virgins slept, all ten woke, all ten trimmed their lamps, and the trimming of the foolish is what revealed that they had no oil. Outward preparation performed at the last hour cannot supply what was never there. And 2 Samuel 19 shows the opposite and rarer thing: a man who did not trim at all for weeks, whose neglected beard was his evidence of loyalty to an absent king.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew asah (H6213), to do or dress; yatab (H3190), to make good, to trim; Greek kosmeo (G2885), to put in order, to adorn; lampas (G2985), a torch or lamp.

expand to see more

Hebrew asah (H6213) — to do, to make, to dress; Mephibosheth had not dressed his feet.

Hebrew yatab (H3190) — to make good, to make fair; why trimmest thou thy way.

Greek kosmeo (G2885) — to arrange, to put in order, to adorn; the virgins trimmed their lamps.

Greek lampas (G2985) — a torch, a lamp; what all ten possessed and only five could keep lit.

Greek elaion (G1637) — oil; the one thing trimming could not supply.

Usage

"“Nor trimmed his beard... until the day he came again in peace” — loyalty visible."

"“Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love?” — conduct groomed for an audience."

"“Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps” — all ten did."
